answer: Final answer: **p = 0.197 (Wald)** for the BMI coefficient from a full multivariate logistic regression of treatment response (responder = Efficacy=='PR', equivalently Groups==1) on BMI (continuous) + Age + Family history + ECOG-PS + Child-Pugh + Chemotherapy experience + HBV infection + Gender, n = 80 (no missingness, converged with no separation). Wald p = 0.1972 (rounded 0.20); likelihood-ratio cross-check p = 0.1884; univariate sensitivity p = 0.087.
